root_cause: The loop breaks immediately after a "Yes" is printed, causing "No" to also be printed regardless of the condition. The break statement prematurely terminates the loop, leading to incorrect final outputs.
suggestion:
Suggestion 1. Check flag variable to control flow. Instead of directly printing "No":
1. Introduce a boolean flag (e.g., `found`) and set it to `false` initially.
2. When the condition is met (`if (listA.contains(combinedList.get(i)) && listA.contains(combinedList.get(i + 1)))`), set the flag to `true`, then print "Yes" and break the loop.
3. After the loop, check the flag. If it remains `false`, print "No".
This ensures that "No" is printed only if the condition is never met even once.
